name: Vajradeha
body:
Vajradeha
CR 8

This tall, bald man looks like a grotesque statue, horrifically scarred and thickened skin clinging to monstrously bulging muscles that somehow are no hindrance to his fluid movements and cat-like flexibility.

XP 4,800
LN Medium humanoid (human)
Init +5; Senses Perception +16

DEFENSE

AC 24, touch 16, flat-footed 18 (+5 Dex, +1 dodge, +8 natural)
hp 114 (12d8+60)
Fort +13, Ref +11, Will +10; +4 vs. mind-affecting and pain
Defensive Abilities hardened flesh, improved evasion
DR 10/adamantine; Immune disease, poison; Resist acid 5, cold 5, fire 5

OFFENSE

Speed 50 ft., climb 30 ft., swim 30 ft.
Melee 2 slams +17/12 (2d6+7/19-20)
Special Attacks lightning speed

STATISTICS

Str 24, Dex 20, Con 21, Int 11, Wis 18, Cha 7
Base Atk +9; CMB +16; CMD 32
Feats Deflect ArrowsB, Dodge, Endurance, Improved Critical (slam), Iron Will, Lightning Reflexes, Weapon Focus (slam)
Skills Acrobatics +16, Climb +21, Perception +16, Survival +10, Swim +10; Racial Modifiers +8 Acrobatics
Languages Common
SQ extreme endurance

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Extreme Endurance (Ex)

A vajradeha gain double the normal bonus on checks and saves from the Endurance feat (+8 instead of +4).

Hardened Flesh (Ex)

A vajradeha gains a bonus to their natural armor equal to their Constitution modifier (+5 for most vajradehas, for a total of +8 natural armor bonus).

Lightning Speed (Ex)

A vajradeha can make iterative attacks with their slams, making a typical vajradeha able to attack four times in a full attack.

ECOLOGY

Environment any
Organization solitary, pair, group (3–5), school (6–12), or assembly (13+)
Treasure standard

First vajradehas came into being as an extremist order of monks that rejected concepts of spiritual enlightenment and usage of ki, believing peak physical aptitude beyond human constraints to be the correct and pure way to achieving perfection.

Disregarding all scholarly, philosophical and artistic pursuits, vajradehas are not born, but forged. Almost literally having to leave humanity behind, only the most dedicated monks can strive to become a vajradeha. It takes many years of intense training to challenge the mind and body enough for such a transformation, to put it beyond mortal limits. It begins at becoming a pinnacle of athleticism and strength that not many are able to achieve, and then pushing it further, toughening body and skin by an array of techniques, using acid, fire, blunt force and more. They spend all their waking hours either training in the art of combat or using esoteric methods to toughen their sinews, bones and reportedly even internal organs. Most of those that try themselves at this process die, and almost all others have to undergo prolonged exposure to dangerous herbal alchemy to enhance their bodies enough to become a vajradeha. Only a handful of them can claim to achieve this status without such procedures, and those claims are harder still to verify, most scholars shaking their heads at the idea of a man achieving such abilities via training alone. A vajradeha leaps like a tiger, runs like a cheetah, climbs like an ape and swims like a shark. Their skin and muscles are thick and dense enough to shatter spears and stop blades. They can crush a man’s ribcage through a breastplate with a single strike and laugh off a cobra’s bite. They are fast enough to swat arrows out of air and can reportedly kill a man in the time it takes him to open his eyes after he blinks. They seemingly don’t tire, fear nothing, ignore pain and shrug off attempts at mental control.

Despite these inhuman capabilities, vajradehas are often simple beings and many of them lack a clear place in the world. They are socially inept and can barely overcome any challenge other than purely physical. Their pride disallows them from serving foreign lords and their strongly lawful disposition means they very rarely use their strength for personal gain. Most of the vajradehas endlessly train to become even stronger, tougher and more dangerous, seemingly oblivious that it’s impossible to push their bodies much further. Others wander the world, often discovering it for the first time in their life after decades spent at an isolated monastery. These travelers may prove themselves at athletic contests or earn some level of admiration and trust by eliminating various dangers, like scattering gangs of brigands or defeating man-slaying beasts. While vajradehas are as ascetic as many monks, they are also careful to optimize their life around keeping their bodies in peak condition, which often entails getting good sleep and a lot of lean, healthy but also muscle-fueling food. While most of them don’t keep treasures and some of them may not even know the concept of coin, vajradehas may with a silent nod accept a gift of a hearty meal or a roof over their head to spend the night in peace.

Vajradehas most often advance by gaining hit dice, but some especially broad?minded and enlightened ones may revisit the traditional monk training, either accepted back into the fold or seeking to complement their physical prowess with increased skill. Those are most easily represented by the monk simple class template, although adding monk levels from scratch is also a valid option.

An average vajradeha is 6-1/2 feet tall and weighs around 400 pounds.
